lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Greenleaf Florist | Delivery Driver and Shop Assistant | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Delivered 30 to 40 arrangements a day across the city and took cash and card payments at the door.
- Prepared weekend wedding orders with the head florist and kept the cooler stocked and labeled.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Owned the pick-path layouts for the fast-moving zone and the labor reports the shift leads used.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; the findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
- Reduced freight costs by 15% by consolidating supplier pickups into regional milk runs.
- Set reorder points for every SKU from 18 months of daily demand and supplier lead-time data, reviewed monthly with the category managers.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Raised the packaging line's overall equipment effectiveness (OEE) from 71% to 112% by cutting changeover time and micro-stops.
- Cut average order lead time through the warehouse from 10 days to 5 while holding daily throughput constant and doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Modeled a regional grocer's 85 daily delivery stops as a vehicle-routing problem, cutting planned route miles 18% against the grocer's current routes.
- Checked the planned routes against 4 weeks of real delivery logs; planned drive times came within 5% of the actual ones.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Analyzed warehouse operations and made recommendations to the food bank's leadership.
- The donation intake process was mapped and two duplicate data-entry steps were removed, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python
Methods: demand forecasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Experience is not listed in reverse chronology.
items.because: Lakeview appears above the more recent Crestway role, making the section harder to scan.

items.says: Education appears before the more relevant experience and projects.
items.because: Several years of relevant work provide stronger early evidence than the 2014–2018 degree.

items.says: Greenleaf is too prominent beside the operations roles.
items.because: The current delivery role draws attention away from the supply-chain progression and can make the career appear to move backward.

items.says: Skills should follow the relevant experience and projects rather than compete with them near the top.
The delivery and payment work has no stated result.
“Took cash and card payments at the door” is indirect and includes filler.
The wedding-order preparation and cooler work has no stated result.
The pick-path and labor-report responsibilities lack an operational result or measured comparison.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the work improved travel time, labor planning, throughput, or another outcome.

items.says: “Owned the pick-path layouts” does not name the action used to create or improve them.
items.because: The reader cannot distinguish layout analysis and design from maintenance or administration.

items.says: “From 3 days to 1” is grammatically incomplete.
items.because: The final number lacks its unit.

items.says: The strongest Lakeview result should open the entry.
The cycle-counting result is buried in an overloaded duty list.
items.because: Unrelated responsibilities dilute the relevant inventory skill.

items.says: The sentence falsely makes every listed duty appear to have raised inventory accuracy.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether the improvement came from cycle counting or the unrelated duties.

items.says: “Inventory fell by $1.9M” lacks a measurement period or comparison.
items.because: The reader cannot assess the size and meaning of the reduction without that context.

items.says: The strongest demand-planning outcomes are buried after the scope and method.
“By 15% by consolidating” repeats the same construction.
The reorder-point activity has no stated operational result.
items.because: The data source and review process show method, but not whether stockouts, inventory, or service improved.

items.says: “Reviewed monthly” does not identify what was reviewed.
items.because: It could refer to the reorder points or the underlying data.

items.says: The supplier scorecard bullet stops at a follow-on activity rather than a supplier-performance result.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether on-time delivery, lead times, or reliability improved.

items.says: “The five least reliable” leaves the affected vendors less explicit.
Standard OEE cannot rise to 112%.
items.because: Its availability, performance, and quality components are each capped at 100%.

items.says: The bullet names changeover time and micro-stops but not the interventions.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what operational change produced the claimed result.

items.says: The lead-time, throughput, and work-in-process claims contradict Little’s law.
items.because: At constant throughput, halving lead time should halve WIP, not double it.

items.says: The warehouse-flow intervention is unclear.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what changed in warehouse flow or release planning.

items.says: “To keep pickers busy” is informal.
items.because: It makes doubling WIP sound like an unexplained staffing tactic.

items.says: The routing bullet does not say how the vehicle-routing problem was solved.
“Cutting planned route miles 18% against” is an awkward comparison.
“The actual ones” is vague.
The pilot adoption has no measured operational result.
items.because: The truck count and duration show scale, not whether the pilot confirmed savings or improved operations.

items.says: The opening analysis statement is generic and shows no adoption, change, or outcome.
items.because: It does not identify the process examined or show whether the recommendations were useful.

items.says: The opening analysis bullet has no measurement of the problem, recommendation, or outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot judge the issue’s scale or the value of the team’s work.

items.says: The donation-intake bullet should name the team’s actions directly and lead with the one-day result.
The forecasting results lack a comparison period.
items.because: “More than halved stockouts” does not say when the comparison was measured.

items.says: The nearly $2M inventory figure does not say what it measures.
The wording makes the forecast appear to cause the results grammatically.
items.because: “That” modifies “forecast,” obscuring the distinction between the team’s action and its outcomes.

items.says: The entry repeats an achievement already claimed under Crestway Foods.
items.because: Both bullets describe forecasting about 1,400 items across three facilities with similar stockout and inventory results.
